# OS Folder Guidance

- `.os/` is for personal PC setup, bootstrap workflows, and reusable machine tooling.
- This folder is not Smash-specific product code by default.
- Prefer placing keybinding-target scripts under `.os/scripts/keybindings/` to make intent discoverable.
- Machine setup is one list, `.os/machine.toml` (packages, Omarchy settings, bar options, Hyprland toggles,
  plugins, files, web apps), plus the real files in `.os/files/`. `os sync` makes the machine and the list
  the same in both directions: it asks what to do with each change made on the machine (keep = save to the
  list, discard = undo here), applies what came from the list, then commits and pushes `.os/`. See
  `.os/README.md`.
- After changing something `os sync` tracks (eg `$HOME/.config/hypr/bindings.lua`, an installed or removed
  package, a web app, the theme, a toggle), record it right away with
  `uv run .os/cli.py keep <kind>:<name> ...` (kinds: `package`, `plugin`, `webapp`, `file`, `setting`,
  `toggle`, `bar`; `--dry-run` previews). It is the no-questions form of answering "keep" in `os sync`: it
  saves this machine's current state of the named things into `.os/machine.toml` / `.os/files/` and does
  nothing else (no pull, commit or push). Prefer it over editing those by hand. Then tell the user what was
  recorded; `os sync` (or a commit and push, when they ask) sends it to the other machines. Never leave the
  machine and the list out of sync.
- `keep` refuses when the list has a version this machine has not synced (or the machine never synced and
  differs): saving would undo the other machine's change. Don't force it; tell the user to run `os sync`.
  Don't run `os sync` for the user without `--dry-run`: it asks questions and changes the machine.
- `keep file:<path under $HOME>` on a path not yet under `[files]` starts tracking it. For something wanted
  on this machine only, add it to `[ignore]` (packages, web apps) instead of keeping it.
- `os sync` applies through the Omarchy CLI (`omarchy pkg add`, `omarchy webapp install`, `omarchy theme set`,
  ...) and only copies plain files for the user-owned ones listed under `[files]`. Keep it that way: don't
  write Omarchy's own state files directly, and never edit `/usr/share/omarchy/`.
- Packages: `[packages]` in `.os/machine.toml` (`pacman` or `aur`). `[ignore]` lists packages and web apps
  that are never synced (hardware-specific, part of Omarchy, or wanted on one machine only).
- To track another file, add `"<path under $HOME>" = "always"` under `[files]`; the next `os sync` saves it.
  For a machine-specific file use `"lspci:<text>"` (hardware), not the hostname; every fresh Omarchy install
  is named `omarchy`.
- Tracked files must work on every machine: use `$HOME` / `os.getenv("HOME")`, not `/home/<user>`.
- Never put secrets in `.os/`; passwords live in the per-machine keyring (`os pwd-store`).
- `.os/install.sh` is plain bash on purpose (an exception to the Typer + shell wrapper pattern): it runs
  before `uv` exists on a fresh machine. It installs `uv`, runs the root `.install.sh` (the delulu-smash
  framework: Python environment, git-lfs data), then `os sync`. Keep it minimal; logic belongs in
  `.os/cli.py`, and framework install steps belong in the root `.install.sh`.
- Keybindings: check the live bindings with `omarchy menu keybindings --print` first. If a key is taken,
  `hl.unbind` it, add a `-- previously: <default>` comment, and tell the user what it replaced.
- Favor portability across the user's Linux machines, especially Omarchy-based systems.
- Prefer `$HOME`-relative paths over hardcoded `/home/<user>` paths when writing scripts, keybindings, or setup examples intended to work on multiple machines.
- Keep setup assumptions explicit: dependencies, output paths, and intended usage should be easy to recover later.
- Prefer concise purpose headers in scripts and straightforward setup documentation in markdown files.
